nv_romper_room.blurb: Romper Room is a small sandstone crag in First Creek Canyon in Red Rock, reached on foot from the canyon trail. It holds about a dozen short single-pitch lines, mostly traditional with a few set up for top-roping. Grades start in the easy 5.5 range, cluster around 5.6 to 5.8, and top out with a couple of 5.10 lines, which makes it a friendly place for newer leaders building mileage on gear. The wall faces northeast, so it catches the morning sun. Descents are generally by rappel, and some lines call for two ropes. The soft sandstone is easily damaged when damp, so pick a dry spell.

nv_tsunami_wall.blurb: Tsunami Wall is a steep, varnished sandstone panel in the Calico Hills area of Red Rock, just outside Las Vegas. It is a sport crag with a dozen climbs: nearly all bolted, plus a lone easy trad line. The bolted routes are short and crimpy on an overhanging face, and the grades skew hard, with a couple of 5.10s and then a large block of 5.12s and a few 5.13s. It is a spot for strong climbers rather than beginners. The face stays out of the sun until late morning and gets it through the afternoon. Wet sandstone is fragile, so skip it after rain.

nv_north_breezeway_dome.blurb: North Breezeway Dome is the middle of three domes at The Moon, also called Knob Hill, in the Eldorado Mountains of southern Nevada, close to where people camp. It is an all-trad crag with twelve routes on quartz monzonite, the granite-like rock that Joshua Tree climbers will recognise. The main face looks east and reaches roughly 130 feet at its tallest. Grades run from 5.6 up to 5.11, with most lines between 5.8 and 5.10, so it suits climbers comfortable placing gear on cracks and dihedrals. Expect a remote, quiet desert setting with scrub oak and boulders around the base.

nv_missionary_wall.blurb: Missionary Wall is a large limestone wall in Campsite Canyon in the Mormon Mountains of southern Nevada, and the canyon's easiest place to reach. All twelve climbs are sport routes, with a good run of moderate lines from 5.8 through 5.10, a single 5.6, and one hard route in the 5.12 range. The rock varies from grey, runnelled lower-angle sections to smooth, streaked overhanging stone. The wall stands right beside the camp spot, so there is almost no walking. It is remote and quiet, and you could easily have it to yourself, but the canyon funnels wind so it can feel breezy.
nv_missionary_wall.parking_note: Follow the dirt road into the canyon until it ends at the camping spot; the wall rises directly beside that parking area.

nv_2_moon_sector.blurb: Moon Sector is the left-hand section of the Wall of Misfortune, a northeast-facing sport wall in the Mormon Mountains of southern Nevada. It has twelve bolted routes, all in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, with 5.12 the most common, making it the hardest-concentrated part of the wall. Most lines start with a steep or slightly overhanging crux and ease to a slab above. The sector picks up sun only for a few morning hours in the main season, so it stays fairly cool. It is a destination for strong sport climbers, a remote and uncrowded place.
nv_2_moon_sector.approach: Hike the trail to the Sun Kissed sector, then keep going left along the base of the wall for roughly ten more minutes.

nv_outback_boulder.blurb: Outback Boulder is a lone sandstone boulder tucked into a shallow bowl on the edge of the Kraft boulder zone in Gateway Canyon, Red Rock. It feels secluded, and the surrounding canyon runs cooler and shadier than the busier boulders beyond. About a dozen problems cover a nice range, from V0 warm-ups through the middle grades to a couple of V5s. Nearly all of them are highball, and the stone is soft, so a few lines feel sketchy. Bring pads and spotters, and pack out any waste. Climbing on damp sandstone damages it, so wait for dry ground.
